reason: The text fragment does not contain any depiction of Yahweh at all. This passage (Exodus 1:6-12 in the Hebrew Masoretic text) describes the death of Joseph and his generation, the rise of a new Egyptian Pharaoh, and the Egyptians' political and military concerns about the growing Israelite population. The entire narrative is told from a human, earthly perspective focusing on Egyptian decisions and actions. There is no mention of God, no divine characterization, and no theological depiction of any deity in this passage.
